findings.evidence: If the position counts as full-time, the stipend can apply. If the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, the stipend can apply. If the request arrives before the benefit year ends, the stipend can apply. Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available to the employee.
findings.fix: State the governing rule first: 'The home-office equipment stipend is available when all three conditions are met: the position is full-time, the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, and the request arrives before the benefit year ends.'
findings.violation: The passage opens with three sentences of conditions and exceptions before the fourth sentence finally states what the benefit actually is, so a reader has to reach the end before the opening sentences make sense.

findings.evidence: 36-word sentence, 4 subordinate-clause markers: Then, the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email.
findings.fix: Split the sentence at a subordinate-clause boundary.
findings.violation: The sentence runs to 36 words with 4 subordinate-clause markers, longer than the reader can hold in mind on a single pass.

findings.evidence: Terminology Notes section (lines 50-53): Sentence 1 subject: 'You' (employee); Sentence 2 subject: 'Finance'; Sentence 3 subject: 'Payroll'; Sentence 4 subject: 'You' (employee); Sentence 5 subject: 'You' (employee). The passage jumps between employee, Finance, and Payroll perspectives without clear connections.
findings.fix: Restructure this section with consistent subject focus. Either describe all steps from the employee's perspective, or clearly separate employee actions from backend processes.
findings.violation: The passage's subjects shift in nearly every sentence (You -> Finance -> Payroll -> You -> You), so the reader has to re-orient at nearly every boundary with no sentence picking up the topic the one before it established.

findings.evidence: The request is reviewed within two business days.
findings.fix: Rewrite the sentence in active voice, naming the actor that performs the action.
findings.violation: The sentence uses a be-verb plus past-participle passive construction in a context where the actor is recoverable and worth naming directly.

findings.evidence: Also, the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time.
findings.fix: Replace the wordy phrase with its plain equivalent (for example, because for due to the fact that, and remove at this point in time).
findings.violation: The sentence uses wordy constructions from the fixed wordy-phrase list that shorter equivalents would carry with no loss of meaning.

findings.evidence: Program Overview (line 2): 'The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter.' Overview section (line 59): 'The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period.' Program Coordination (line 63): 'The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout.' These terms are used interchangeably without established equivalence.
findings.fix: Define the relationship between these teams (e.g., state whether the benefits team is part of the people operations office) or use a consistent term throughout the document.
findings.location: Program Overview, Overview section, and Program Coordination
findings.violation: Two terms that refer to the identical entity are used interchangeably across the document with no signal that they mean the same thing, forcing the reader to determine whether these are one team or two.

findings.evidence: However, reimbursement is not available without a completed receipt.
findings.fix: Restate the sentence with at most one negation, or recast it as a positive statement.
findings.violation: 2 negation markers from the fixed negation list co-occur in one clause, so the reader has to work out the statement's logical sign before understanding it.

findings.fix: Replace the heading with text specific enough to be found by scanning.
findings.violation: The heading text matches the fixed list of non-specific heading labels, so a reader scanning headings cannot tell whether the section applies to them.
